sections.h2: Where is Rosemount, Minnesota, and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Twenty miles south of Saint Paul, Rosemount marks the southern fringe of the metro in Dakota County, with the Mississippi River touching its northeast corner. The Census Bureau lists 33.25 square miles of land. About 7 percent of residents lived in rural areas at the 2020 census.

Settlers began arriving after the 1851 Treaty of Mendota. A postmaster appointed in 1854 named the post office after a town in Ireland, and the township was organized in 1858. Dodd Road, one of the state's early roads, crossed the western part of the township, and a railroad station and elevator in the 1860s pulled a commercial center toward the tracks. The village was platted in 1866 and incorporated in 1875.

The 20th century added two large land uses. A wartime gunpowder plant, the Gopher Ordnance Works, was later partly acquired by the University of Minnesota in 1947 and is now known as UMore Park. The Pine Bend refinery, built in 1955 on the border with Inver Grove Heights, is now owned by Flint Hills Resources and is the area's largest private employer.

sections.h2: How big has Rosemount become, and what do Census figures say about its homes?
sections.html:
Growth here has been fast. The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 31,881 residents, which is 24.3 percent above the 2020 base of 25,651 and far above the 21,874 counted in 2010.

Rosemount is a city of owners: 87.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and 91.5 percent of residents stayed put through the prior year. Children under 18 are 26.5 percent of the population, and 51.6 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or more.

sections.h2: What do the roads, schools and employers mean for a Rosemount seller?
sections.html:
U.S. Highway 52, Minnesota Highways 3 and 55, and County Road 42 are four of the main routes. The Census Bureau puts the average commute at 28.1 minutes, so buyers weigh drive times to Saint Paul, Minneapolis and Dakota County job centers when they look.

Independent School District 196, the Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan district, serves the city. Its Rosemount schools include Emerald Trail, Rosemount and Shannon Park elementaries, Rosemount Middle School and Rosemount High School. Dakota County Technical College is also in the city, and Saint Joseph Catholic School and Rosemount First Baptist School are private options.

Transportation and warehousing is a sizable sector here. The Census Bureau's 2022 figures show $271.7 million in transportation and warehousing receipts, compared with $140.8 million in retail sales.

sections.h2: Does Rosemount require a license to rent out a house?
sections.html:
Yes. The City Code requires a rental dwelling license under Title 9-8-4, and the housing official may inspect the property under Title 9-8-8. The city's application asks whether the building is a single-family home, duplex, townhome or multi-family structure, and whether the license is new or a renewal.

  • An owner who rents out properties in other Minnesota cities must list them on the form.
  • A false statement on the application can lead to suspension or revocation.
  • The application lists a fee of $100 per unit when mailed, so call City Hall at 651-322-2024 to confirm the current amount.

For a house sold with a tenant inside, ask City Hall what happens to the license. The city's website now sits at rosemountmn.gov, and City Hall is at 2875 145th Street West.

sections.h2: How are Dakota County values set, and when can a Rosemount owner appeal?
sections.html:
The county says the road from sales data to a final tax bill takes more than three years. Sales from October 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025 formed the basis for the 2026 assessment, which uses a January 2, 2026 market value for taxes payable in 2027. Notices went to every owner in March 2026, and the appeal window ran March through May.

Once the special county board adjourned on June 8, 2026, state law barred Assessing Services from changing the 2026 value. What remains is a Minnesota Tax Court petition, which has an April 30 deadline in the year the tax is payable. The county takes service of petitions at taxpetitions@co.dakota.mn.us or in person in Hastings.

The proposed statements are arriving this month. Gather recent sales of similar houses if you plan to question next year's value, and call Assessing Services at 651-438-4200.

sections.h2: What does Dakota County need when a Rosemount deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Recording for Dakota County happens at Property Taxation and Records, 1590 Highway 55, Hastings. The office takes deeds at an appointment or through the mail, and a mailed package needs a cover letter, a stamped return envelope and a daytime phone number. Expect the originals back within one to two weeks.

  • The county lists a $46 fee for an abstract document, plus a $5 conservation fee on instruments where deed tax was paid.
  • Card payments for recordings carry a 2.49 percent service charge.
  • Every transfer deed needs a well disclosure certificate, or one of two statements about wells printed on the deed.

Most Dakota County land is abstract property, which means a title company searches the records at sale. Torrens property instead has a certificate of title. The county's property search shows which type applies to your parcel. Dakota County staff will not help fill in legal forms, so rely on a closing agent or an attorney.

sections.h2: What is the certificate of real estate value?
sections.html:
Minn. Stat. 272.115 requires a certificate of value for any sale over $3,000. The seller, buyer or an agent files it with the Dakota County auditor as the deed is presented, and it reports financing terms and nets out personal property sold along with the house.

The same section blocks homestead classification in the years after a sale when no certificate was filed, so ask your closing agent to confirm it goes in with the deed.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a Rosemount house?
sections.html:
The Dakota County paperwork above applies on every route, and three are common in a city like this one.

  • An agent listing suits a ready house and a calendar that allows for showings.
  • A sale handled without an agent leaves the disclosure, certificate of value and well disclosure to the seller.
  • An as-is cash purchase fits a rental, an estate property or a house that needs more work than the owner wants to do.

Whichever route you take, write down material facts for the buyer, learn whether the parcel is abstract or Torrens, and have the closing agent send the deed, well disclosure and certificate of value together.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a house I have been renting out in Rosemount?
faqs.a: The license applies to operating a rental, so ask City Hall at 651-322-2024 what to do with it when the house changes hands. Rosemount's Title 9-8-4 requires the license, and the housing official can inspect under Title 9-8-8.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Dakota County assessment still open to appeal?
faqs.a: Not through the county, since its special board finished on June 8, 2026. A Tax Court petition stays possible until April 30 of the payable year.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Rosemount house?
faqs.a: Dakota County Property Taxation and Records in Hastings records it. You can book an appointment, or mail the deed, the fees, a cover letter and a self-addressed stamped envelope to 1590 Highway 55.

faqs.q: What is a well disclosure on a Minnesota deed?
faqs.a: Dakota County wants to know about wells on every parcel that changes hands. The deed travels with a completed certificate and fee, or with a printed sentence saying the seller knows of no wells or that nothing has changed since the last certificate.

faqs.q: When will my next Dakota County property tax statements arrive?
faqs.a: Proposed statements for 2027 go out in November 2026, and the final statements follow in March 2027. The first half is due in May 2027 and the second half in October 2027.
